newsitem.title: FRANCE: Borotra seeks re-allocation of job aid spending.
newsitem.headline: Borotra seeks re-allocation of job aid spending.

text.p: Industry Minister Franck Borotra said in a newspaper interview published on Friday that he proposed to slash the 120 billion francs spent annually on aid to employment to 60 billion francs, and use 30 billion francs to lower payroll charges and 30 billion to reduce the deficit.
He said the 120 billion francs currently spent to spur job creation was not the most efficient use of that money.

"We spend 120 billion francs on aid to employment. We need to reduce that by 60 billion francs and allocate 30 billion to reduce charges and the other 30 billion to cut the deficit," Borotra told the newspaper Les Echos.

He said one of the big differences between the Right and the Left was that the Left was proposing policies of redistribution while the Right viewed growth as the best solution to France's economic problems.
"First, we need an industrial priority," he said. "Then, we need to reinforce the competitiveness of companies by reducing the charges that burden labour costs."
